: Reader tasks by status. {#tbl-appg-reader-tasks}

## Answered {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- Choose between the pip install and a source build. See [Install and run](#sec-preface-install).
- Understand what a finite-volume method is and why cell values are averages. See The finite-volume update and the flux divergence, @sec-ch04-divergence.
- Find the time order of the combined implicit/explicit step and its derivation. See Stage-weighted implicit step: the correction runs with $w_2^{(s)}\Delta t$ under rk3 and rk3s4, @sec-ch07-vic-stage.
- List the reconstructions and limiters with stencil width, ghost count and defaults. See The reconstruction framework, @sec-ch04-framework.
- Understand how the hydrostatic state is preserved and which reference is subtracted. See Well-balanced $x_1$ reconstruction: perturbations about a hydrostatic reference (gravity on), @sec-ch05-wbx1.
- Check whether reconstruction accounts for stretched or curvilinear spacing and what order it reaches. See The reconstruction framework, @sec-ch04-framework.
- List the time integrators with key names, stage counts and SSP coefficients. See Explicit SSP Runge-Kutta stages in Shu-Osher form, @sec-ch07-rk.
- Check whether density and pressure positivity is guaranteed and what happens when it fails. See The equation-of-state limiter: two passes, floors and marks, @sec-ch08-eoslimiter.
- Find how radiation is coupled to the dynamics. See Locate dependencies outside snapy, @sec-ch01-dependencies.
- Understand how kintera and pyharp plug in and whether my first run needs them. See External component interfaces, @sec-appe-components.
- Understand precipitation and sedimentation: fall speed, time-step limit, budget at the bottom. See Sedimentation of condensates, @sec-ch10-sed.
- Open a NetCDF output file in Python and plot temperature. See NetCDF output: per-block files and the combine, @sec-ch14-netcdf.
- Understand how output is written across processes and its limits. See NetCDF output: per-block files and the combine, @sec-ch14-netcdf.

- Add sedimentation or precipitation for a condensate and see how it limits the step. See Sedimentation of condensates, @sec-ch10-sed.
- Look up the state-vector layout and the units of condensates. See [2. State, thermodynamics and species](#sec-appa-2).

- Check bitwise reproducibility across CPU/GPU, threads and ranks. See Reproducibility: what is shown bit for bit and what is not, @sec-ch14-repro.

- Add a reconstruction or Riemann solver in C++ and select it from YAML. See The reconstruction framework, @sec-ch04-framework.

## Undocumented {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- Set up a problem of my own (e.g. a warm bubble in a chosen atmosphere) starting from an example. Not provided: no problem-design tutorial; only the initial-state contract exists (@sec-ch01-initialization).
- Find how Coriolis and geometric sources interact with the well-balanced reconstruction. Not provided: no section states the interaction.
- List the numerical dissipation of the scheme (Riemann solver, limiters) apart from physical diffusion. Not provided: no list of numerical dissipation and no physical-vs-numerical split.
- Identify the latest usable checkpoint after a node or storage failure. Not provided: the book states no completeness guarantee for an interrupted write and no procedure for finding the latest usable checkpoint after a failure.
- Record what a paper needs: code version, resolved configuration, dependencies, hardware. Not provided: no publication-record checklist; output does not record a resolved configuration.
- Compare thermodynamic constants with sources against my old model. Not provided: saturation vapour pressures not covered; deck values cited only to deck lines; cv_R=2.5 unsourced.
- Find which results-changing fixes went into which versions. Not provided: no per-version list of results-changing fixes.
- Cite snapy and the document for the numerics of a version. Not provided: no citation guidance or reference list.
- Estimate device and host memory before a production run and reduce it. Not provided: no memory estimate at the pin.
- Find a performance baseline for each release. Not provided: no performance baseline for any release.
- Run a 1-D shock tube example. Not provided: no shock-tube (Sod) deck or card in the book.
- Relate cubed-sphere panel orientation to FV3 or MITgcm. Not provided: the panel frame is defined in @sec-ch03-gnomonic, but there is no mapping to FV3 or MITgcm panel numbering or orientation.
- Understand the pole treatment on the spherical-polar grid. Not provided: no section treats the poles; @sec-ch03-sphpolar only requires x2 within [0, pi]; "pole" occurs once, in @sec-ch03-synctype ("away from a pole").
- Restart a run from a NetCDF dump. Not provided: restart reads only .restart bundles (load_pt_from_bundle, @sec-ch14-restart); no reader starts a run from a NetCDF output file.

## Outside scope {.unnumbered .unlisted}

- Ask a question or report a reproducible bug. Not provided: a bug-report and support procedure is a tutorial.
- Tell whether a feature is physics or a numerical artifact. Not provided: telling physics from numerical artifacts is a tutorial/science study.
- Open the output, plot one variable and make an animation. Not provided: plotting and animating output is a tutorial, which this report on the code does not give.
- Run a standard cross-model test (Held-Suarez-like, Jupiter jet) to validate a port. Not provided: cross-model benchmarks are a science study.
- Triage a disagreement with my old model: physics, numerics, resolution or conversion. Not provided: triaging a disagreement with another model is a tutorial, which this report on the code does not give.
- Estimate spin-up time of a Jupiter-like run and accelerate it. Not provided: spin-up is a science study.
- Check how GCM comparisons regrid and match effective resolution. Not provided: regridding and matching effective resolution for comparisons between models is a science study, which this report on the code does not give.
- See the sensitivity of jets and deep winds to damping choices. Not provided: damping sensitivity is a science study.
